newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ANI sells three Holter operations.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ANI sells three Holter operations.

text.p: Australian National Industries said on Friday it had completed negotiations to sell three operations of its Holter environmental engineering operation based in Germany. The sales occurred at above book value, ANI said.
ANI said it would sell Holter's half share in SHU Saarberg-Holter Umwelttechnik GmbH and 100 percent of Holter/ABT's industrial filter business to Saarbergwerke Ag for 35 million marks in cash.
Saarberg owns the other 50 percent of SHU.
It said it would sell its half share in UTR Umwelt-Technologie und Recycling GmbH to partner Ruhrkohle AG for 3.3 million marks.
"The total value of the sale of these assets modestly exceeds ANI's book value," ANI said.
ANI managing director Peter Stancliffe said SHU and UTR were modestly profitable and mature businesses but they did not offer long term strategic value to the Australian company.

ANI also said as part of the Holter restructuring process, it had decided not to extend the option expiry date under which it could buyback 50 percent of the Saarberg-Holter Wassertechnik (SHW) waste water treatment business in Germany. The remainder of SHW is held by Saarberg and the option expired on October 31.
The overall Hotler operations have drained ANI's profits in recent years, costing the parent more than A$200 million.
